doc.title: Charles Lloyd — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Higgins, Hendrix and the spiritual path
title: Swimming, ping-pong and Ornette's oatmeal cookies
summary: Lloyd talks about being a Memphis diving champion, ping-pong at the YMCA, and Ornette and he sharing cheese and cookies while playing.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I used to be a tennis player, an athlete and stuff.

I was a swimmer, I was a junior Olympic swimming champion. My wife’s ­ Dorothy’s - Oh. I wasn’t a junior Olympic swimmer. She was a junior Olympic swimming champ! That’s why you can’t give yourself roses.
Because you pat yourself on the back, you might hit a tree. You know, so I mess up. But I was a diving champion.

Yeah, I could do stuff. But anyway, the reason I’m rough on the ping pong table is because there was a YMCA near us, and there’d be twenty little boys lined up to play the next guy who won. So if you lose, you gotta wait for two more hours, for twenty three more hours.
Right, a long time, right. Yeah.

So I had to get my proficiency up. It’s the same thing with music. See, I can play. But Ornette and I used to have a beautiful argument. I’m in college, and I would have been... not pedantic, but I was like - cause I knew the difference - but I would be, you know. So he and I would be arguing. I said, “Well, Ornette...” and we couldn’t put two nickels together that could buy us some oatmeal cookies and American cheese. So we’d be jammin’ and playin’. But that’s what we would eat. He’d send his wife out to get a quarter’s worth of cheese. We’d all put nickels in and some oatmeal cookies, and we’d make a little sandwich, you know. And we’d keep playin’ four or five more hours, you know. So anyway, he... what was I telling you? Help me out. You guys are in the rhythm section man!
